results.translation: THE HERBALL, OR GENERAL HISTORY OF PLANTS. Gathered by John Gerarde of London, Master in Surgery. Printed at London by John Norton. 1597.
results.confidence_reason: The title page text is printed in clear roman and italic type and is well preserved and legible.
results.translator_notes: An illegible ink inscription appears at the top of the page in a later cursive hand, possibly reading something like 'Ex libris Rachel...' or a similar ownership note; too faint/cursive to confidently transcribe. A pink stamp reading 'Mo. Bot. Garden 1899' (a library accession stamp) appears near the imprint date and is not part of the original text.

results.title_inferred: Heraldic Coat of Arms with Latin Motto (Dedication Page)
results.original_text:
HONI SOIT QUI MAL Y PENSE

COR VNVM, VIA VNA.

Quot descripta vides (Mecœnas) nomina florum,
Mυειάδας εξαθῶν tot tibi mente precor.
results.translation:
Shame on him who thinks evil of it (the Order of the Garter motto)

One heart, one way.

As many named flowers as you see described here, Patron,
So many myriads [of blessings] I wish you with my whole mind.
results.confidence_reason: The heraldic motto and Latin verses are clear, but the small Greek phrase and fine details of the woodcut inscription are difficult to render with full certainty.
results.translator_notes: The image shows an elaborate heraldic achievement (coat of arms with supporters of two lions, a helm, and crest) surrounded by the Garter motto 'HONI SOIT QUI MAL Y PENSE'. Below the shield is the motto 'COR VNVM, VIA VNA' (One heart, one way). Beneath the woodcut is a Latin distich addressed to a patron (Mecoenas), with a partial Greek phrase inserted, likely a scribal or printer's flourish. A faint pink stamp/label appears on the shield area but is illegible and appears to be a later library marking, not part of the original text.
